name: calc-evolution
description: Three checkpoints of a tiny TypeScript calculator library: add/negate at T0, subtract introduced at T1, negate removed and VERSION bumped to 2.0.0 at T2. The ledger is a complete census of every material fact about the library at each checkpoint (identity, layout, module locations, exports, typing, purity, docs, per-function behavior, version value), not a list of deltas, so precision is measured against everything true rather than a thin sample. Exercises discovery, retention, complete forgetting, and changed-knowledge correction.

versions.statement: The repository is `calc`, a tiny calculator (arithmetic) library.
The library is written in TypeScript and every public value (the functions and the VERSION constant) is an ES module named export, imported individually; there is no default export.
All source code lives under a top-level `src/` directory.
The arithmetic functions are defined in the module `src/calc.ts`.
The library's version string is defined in its own module, `src/version.ts`, separate from the arithmetic code.
A root `README.md` documents the current version and the public API, listing each function as a bullet under an `## API` heading.
Every exported function carries a JSDoc comment documenting each parameter and its return value.
Every exported function is pure: it performs no input validation, no rounding, and no I/O, and returns a value computed only from its arguments.
Every arithmetic function takes and returns TypeScript `number` values.
`add(a, b)` returns the sum of its two number arguments.
`negate(x)` returns the additive inverse (negation) of its single argument.
`subtract(a, b)` returns the difference of its two arguments, the first minus the second (`a - b`).
The exported VERSION constant is the string "1.0.0", and the README states the library version is 1.0.0.
The exported VERSION constant is the string "2.0.0", and the README states the library version is 2.0.0.
